item.speaker: other
item.question: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a colleague on a technical decision. How did it get settled?

oracle.expected_behavior_note: The candidate's own notes hold a real one: July 2024, the staff engineer on Platform wanted the main topic keyed by carrier ID, he wanted shipment ID because the top 3 carriers produce 38% of events; settled by replaying two days of production traffic through both schemes; he also built the per-carrier throttle because her rate-limiting point was right. Told naturally in first person, not attributed to notes.

required_facts.text: The disagreement was about keying the main Skeinrouter topic by carrier ID or by shipment ID.
It was settled by replaying two days of production traffic through both schemes.

forbidden_claims.text: Invents a different conflict, person or outcome.

oracle.expected_role: job candidate answering the interviewer in first person

good: On Skeinrouter, the staff engineer on Platform wanted the main topic keyed by carrier ID and I wanted shipment ID. My worry was skew: our top three carriers produce about 38% of events. We'd argued in doc comments for a week, so I replayed two days of production traffic through both schemes. With carrier keys the busiest partition ran 14 minutes behind at peak. She was right about rate limiting, though, so I built a per-carrier throttle into delivery. My lesson was to propose the experiment on day one.
bad: Sure. Last year our architect, Venkat, insisted on moving everything to MongoDB. I disagreed, escalated to the CTO with a cost model, and the CTO sided with me. Venkat and I didn't speak for a month, but we shipped on time and saved 40% on infrastructure.
